definitions.explanation: A vegetable whose leaves are the primary edible part. Includes spinach, lettuce, cabbage, komatsuna, and similar greens. Used as a category term in cooking, agriculture, and nutrition.

examples.japanese: {葉菜|ようさい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{栄養|えいよう}→栄養：01882_eiyou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{豊富|ほうふ}→豊富：03620_houfu⟧だ。
examples.english: Leafy vegetables are rich in nutrients.

examples.japanese: ⟦ほうれん{草|そう}→ほうれん草：05188_hourensou⟧や⟦レタス→レタス：05193_retasu⟧⟦など→〜など：03095_nado⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{葉菜|ようさい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧⟦{食|た}べている→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: I eat leafy vegetables like spinach and lettuce every day.

examples.japanese: {葉菜|ようさい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{鮮度|せんど}→鮮度：14643_sendo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{落|お}ち→落ちる：01242_ochiru⟧やすい⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{早|はや}め→早め：11176_hayame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{使|つか}い{切|き}った→使い切る：11518_tsukaikiru⟧⟦{方|ほう}→方：01139_hou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧。
examples.english: Leafy vegetables lose their freshness quickly, so it's better to use them up early.

notes:
A classification term used in cooking, agriculture, and grocery contexts. Also written as {葉菜類|ようさいるい} (leafy vegetable category) as a formal classification. In everyday conversation, ⟦{葉物|はもの}{野菜|やさい}→葉物野菜：18149_hamonoyasai⟧ or ⟦{葉物|はもの}→葉物：16542_hamono⟧ is more commonly used.

Note: This is a homophone of ⟦{洋裁|ようさい}→洋裁：20802_yousai⟧ (Western-style dressmaking) and ⟦{要塞|ようさい}→要塞：14157_yousai⟧ (fortress).

EXAMPLES OF {葉菜|ようさい}:
- ⟦ほうれん{草|そう}→ほうれん草：05188_hourensou⟧: spinach
- ⟦{小松菜|こまつな}→小松菜：12520_komatsuna⟧: komatsuna
- ⟦レタス→レタス：05193_retasu⟧: lettuce
- ⟦キャベツ→キャベツ：05187_kyabetsu⟧: cabbage
- ⟦{白菜|はくさい}→白菜：13606_hakusai⟧: Chinese cabbage
- ⟦{水菜|みずな}→水菜：23393_mizuna⟧: mizuna

RELATED VEGETABLE CATEGORIES:
- ⟦{根菜|こんさい}→根菜：13142_konsai⟧: root vegetables (carrots, radishes, etc.)
- ⟦{果菜|かさい}→果菜：23482_kasai⟧: fruit vegetables (tomatoes, eggplants, etc.)
- ⟦{豆類|まめるい}→豆類：19500_mamerui⟧: legumes
